records.issue_text: The added time.sleep(0.1) for drift propagation in test_consumer.py is a no-op because monkeypatch.setattr('time.sleep', lambda _: None) replaces the sleep attribute on the time module itself, so the race it claims to fix is not mitigated
records.rationale: In `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`, `test_basic` does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` and later adds `time.sleep(0.1)` to “give flusher threads time to process”. Because the test patches `time.sleep` itself, the later `time.sleep(0.1)` call is also replaced with the no-op lambda, so it cannot provide any delay and does not mitigate the claimed race.

records.issue_text: The per-process join loop in flusher.py join() applies the deadline sequentially, so a hung first process consumes the entire timeout leaving zero drain time for remaining processes
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, a single `deadline = time.time() + timeout` is computed once, then processes are handled in a `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` loop. If the first process remains alive until the deadline, the inner loop exits when `deadline <= time.time()`, and the next iteration immediately does `remaining_time = deadline - time.time(); if remaining_time <= 0: break`, which stops processing further processes entirely. This means later processes get no wait time and (worse) are not even `terminate()`d because termination happens inside the per-process loop after t
